research.title: Mechanisms Limiting Long-Run Entanglement Attempt Rates: Cooling, Detector Recovery, Signalling and Covert Scheduling

scope.question: Which physical or operational mechanisms limit the long-run average number of entanglement-generation attempts in a quantum network link over many time slots (for example source duty cycle, ion heating and recooling, detector recovery, or covertness against a warden), as opposed to limits within a single attempt?

criterion.criterion: The paper itself identifies and analyzes a physical or operational mechanism that limits the long-run average rate or number of entanglement-generation attempts in a quantum network link over many time slots, as distinct from limits within a single attempt.

parts.definition: The paper states that the average number or rate of entanglement-generation attempts over many time slots is bounded or constrained, and treats this as a time-averaged quantity rather than the success probability or fidelity of one attempt.
parts.name: Long-run attempt-rate limit

parts.definition: The paper itself names and analyzes a specific physical or operational mechanism that causes the attempt limit, such as source duty cycle, ion heating and recooling, detector dead time or recovery, or a covertness constraint against a warden; a mere mention of the mechanism does not meet it.
parts.name: Limiting mechanism

parts.definition: The paper reports which mechanism applies and how it quantitatively limits the average attempt rate, for example as a duty-cycle bound, cooling time per attempt or detection-recovery delay.
parts.name: Mechanism type and quantification

limitations.text: The covertness scheduler, the batch-separation tools and the multi-atom cavity proposal are known here only from abstracts. Their quantitative effects on the long-run attempt rate could not be checked.

This answer treats a long-run limit as any overhead that recurs between attempts and lowers the average attempt rate over many slots, such as cooling breaks, repumping, reinitialization, detector recovery, reset, waiting for heralds and duty-cycle scheduling. It treats the duration of one attempt as a single-attempt limit.
The attempt-loop and cooling timings in one trapped-ion experiment come from model-read page text and should be checked against the PDF page.
The covertness source states that duty cycle and burst size are adapted to stay below a detection threshold. It gives no figure for how much this lowers the attempt rate.
The batch-separation source is a dataset record that accompanies a paper, not the paper itself. A second record of the same dataset was not cited separately.
